findings.finding: The company is under a 45-day lock-up from the 2026-09-17 underwriting agreement (to about 2026-11-01), so its existing $2,625,000 Cantor at-the-market program cannot be drawn tonight or tomorrow, removing the commonest overnight second leg for a sub-$5 post-merger name.
findings.mechanism_in_window: It bears on the window because an ATM draw is the supply that would otherwise land between today's close and the next close; the lock-up runs past the window end, so for the whole window the issuer is not a seller.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior ATM-draw disclosure observed for this issuer; its post-merger falls (09-17, 09-18, 09-25, 09-28, 10-01) all closed lower next day without any issuer supply event, so the absence of an ATM has not stopped the drift before.
findings.why_not_priced: The tape cannot distinguish an issuer that can sell into a bounce from one that cannot; if a draw were possible the bounce would be capped by $2.6m of ready paper, which against ~$1.1m of median daily turnover would be visible. The fact is small because the remaining ATM capacity is undisclosed and the seller driving the fall is not the issuer.
findings.independence: The ATM agreement dated 2026-08-26 with Cantor is also referenced in the 2026-08-27 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948864/000149315226040292/form8-k.htm); no independent source on the lock-up itself.
